stem: During living donor informed consent, which legal counseling point must the coordinator include per standard references?

options.text: It is a federal crime to offer to donate any human organ for anything of value
Financial compensation for organ donation is legally encouraged
Only state law, not federal law, governs organ sales
Vacation packages may be exchanged for organ donation without restriction

explanation.rationale_correct: Living donor education must confirm that the donor understands it is a federal crime to offer to donate any human organ for anything of value, including cash, property, and vacations.

rationale_incorrect.B: Federal law prohibits organ sales and inducements rather than encouraging compensation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Federal law specifically prohibits offering organs for valuable consideration.
rationale_incorrect.D: Vacations and other items of value are explicitly named as prohibited inducements.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 7, Care of Living Donors → F. Elements Included in Education and Informed Consent → 1.d.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: federal crime to offer to donate any human organ for anything of value including … cash, property, and vacations

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 7 → F. Elements Included in Education and Informed Consent → 1.d. (federal crime to offer organ for anything of value); PDF p. 340 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Federal organ-sales prohibition angle distinct from donor decline right (cctc-1074) and separate live donor team (cctc-1045); anchor verified on Cupples p. 340.

stem: A coordinator is updating JC virus teaching for solid-organ recipients. Evaluate the following statements about progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML):

elements.text: JC virus causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy.
PML is typically associated with fever and meningeal signs such as nuchal rigidity.
Onset may occur more than 6 months to several years after transplantation.
PML has been reported in renal, liver, heart, and lung transplant recipients.

explanation.rationale_correct: JC virus causes PML with progressive neurological deficits; onset is typically delayed months to years after transplant; cases are reported across solid-organ groups. PML is a noninflammatory CNS infection not associated with fever or meningeal signs, so statement II is false.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement II is false; statements III and IV are also correct.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement II is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement II is false—PML is not typically associated with fever or nuchal rigidity.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → J. Polyomaviruses → 3. JC virus → a.–b.
primary_anchor.quote_hint: Causes progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy … more than 6 months to several years … not associated with fever or meningeal signs … renal, liver, heart, and lung

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → J. Polyomaviruses → 3. JC virus → a.–b. (PML cause, delayed onset, noninflammatory presentation, multi-organ reports); PDF p. 208 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

stem: When educating the family of a 3-year-old kidney transplant recipient about early vascular complications, which teaching point aligns with standard references?

options.text: Children younger than 5 years are at highest risk for vascular thrombosis from low-flow states
Pediatric recipients older than 12 years have the highest thrombosis risk
Arterial thrombosis in children typically presents with polyuria rather than anuria
Vascular thrombosis never causes graft loss in pediatric kidney recipients

explanation.rationale_correct: Children younger than 5 years are at highest risk for vascular thrombosis secondary to low flow states; arterial thrombosis may present with sudden anuria and is often irreversible, resulting in graft loss.

rationale_incorrect.B: Younger children, not adolescents, are described as highest risk for vascular thrombosis.
rationale_incorrect.C: Arterial thrombosis presents with sudden anuria rather than polyuria.
rationale_incorrect.D: Arterial thrombosis is often irreversible and may result in graft loss.

stem: When counseling a transplant candidate about pretransplant immunizations, why is early vaccination emphasized in standard references?

options.text: Vaccine response may be diminished with organ failure and further reduced after immunosuppression
All live vaccines are preferred immediately after transplantation
Immunizations are unnecessary before transplant if the candidate feels well
Post-transplant vaccines always produce stronger immunity than pretransplant doses

explanation.rationale_correct: Candidates and recipients are at increased infection risk; response to many vaccines is diminished in organ failure, and transplant recipients may have suboptimal vaccination responses due to immunosuppression, so immunizations should be updated before transplantation when possible.

rationale_incorrect.B: Live vaccines require careful timing and are generally avoided after transplant rather than preferred immediately.
rationale_incorrect.C: Early immunization is emphasized because organ failure and later immunosuppression reduce vaccine response.
rationale_incorrect.D: Post-transplant vaccination responses are often suboptimal rather than stronger than pretransplant immunization.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: response to many vaccines is diminished in organ failure … suboptimal response to vaccinations due to their immunosuppressed status … update immunizations prior to transplantation

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → Immunizations → A.2.–4. (diminished vaccine response with organ failure/immunosuppression; update before transplant); PDF p. 180 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Pretransplant vaccine-response angle distinct from live-vaccine interval (cctc-1077) and post-transplant restart timing (cctc-3074); anchor verified on Cupples p. 180.
